sections.relationship: Students guess and then stop. Supposing one speaker is truthful, following the consequences, and switching when a contradiction appears is a complete method.
sections.author_note: Students guess and then stop. Supposing one speaker is truthful, following the consequences, and switching when a contradiction appears is a complete method.

lesson.title: Suppose, then test
text: Pick one speaker and SUPPOSE that person tells the truth.
Then everything that person says is true. Use it to decide others, one step at a time. A liar's statement must be false.
If you reach a contradiction, the supposition was wrong: that speaker is a liar. Start again with that fact.
When every statement agrees with the speaker's type, you have a solution. Check that no other choice works if the question expects one answer.

example.title: Worked example (different people)
prompt: Pip says: "Rue and I are both liars." Rue says nothing. Who is what?
steps: Suppose Pip is truthful. Then Pip is a liar: contradiction.
So Pip is a liar, and "Rue and I are both liars" is false.
Pip IS a liar, so for the statement to be false, Rue must be a truth-teller.
